description:
FILED + FIXED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).

THE BUG.  perl's `isa` and `DOES` are `boolSV(sv_derived_from(...))`, so a
FALSE answer is PL_sv_no -- the EMPTY STRING, which is DEFINED.  PCL's `p-isa`
returned `t` / `nil`, and nil IS undef, so every assertion that compares the
answer against '' failed on definedness while truthiness agreed all the way:

    is UNIVERSAL::isa($vals[$p], $refs[$q]), ($p==$q or $p+$q==1);
    #   got: undef        expected: ''

t/uni/universal.t's 7x7 matrix is 49 such rows, 40 of them false, and it was
the reason a whole `uni/` file looked like a Unicode problem and is not one:
the probe is pure ASCII.

THE ORACLE (perl 5.40.3, probed row by row; universal.c is the reference).
THREE entry points, THREE rules:
  * the METHOD spelling `$o->isa(X)` / `$o->DOES(X)` / `Class->isa(X)`:
    always 1 or '' -- never undef.  (On an UNBLESSED REF it does not return a
    value at all: it dies "Can't call method \"isa\" on unblessed reference".)
  * the INFIX operator `$o isa Class`: always 1 or ''.
  * the FUNCTION spelling `UNIVERSAL::isa(X, Y)` adds perl's own guard,
    verbatim from XS_UNIVERSAL_isa:
        if (!SvOK(sv) || !(SvROK(sv) || (SvPOKp(sv) && SvCUR(sv))))
            XSRETURN_UNDEF;
    so isa(undef,X) / isa(42,X) / isa("",X) are UNDEF, while isa("str",X) and
    isa([],X) are ''.
  * `can` is the one that really answers undef for false -- PCL already did.

THE FIX.  `p-isa` is documented and implemented as BOOLEAN-VALUED (1 / ""),
which is what both the method spelling and the infix operator want; the undef
answers are UNIVERSAL::pl-isa's guard, where perl puts them.  Two callers
existed and both were checked: cl/pcl-test.lisp already asked `p-true-p`;
cl/pcl-xs.lisp's `xs-isa` used a bare CL `if`, which "" satisfies, and now
asks `p-true-p` too.  THAT is the trap in this change -- perl's false is CL's
true.

BARS.  Guard `Pl/t/census-bugs-01.t` row 29 (14 conjuncts in one program, the
expectation byte-copied from perl's own output), inverse-verified FAILING on a
347a46e3 extraction.  Boolean-position probe (if / unless / stmt-if / grep /
&& / || / infix, 10 shapes) identical to perl.  Targeted gate 402 rows green
except the 13 standing pclxs xs rows.  Full sweep + ir-conform + the uni/+op/
companion legs: see the round record.

RESIDUE, filed separately, all PRE-EXISTING and none made worse by this fix:
#1738 (a class-name invocant with no stash: perl's sv_derived_from wants the
stash to exist, PCL answers 1), #1739 (the INFIX operator wants a BLESSED
REFERENCE on the left -- `"Bar" isa Bar` is '' in perl, 1 in PCL),
#1740 (`UNIVERSAL::DOES([], "x")` dies in perl and runs in PCL).

ADDENDUM (s473t5f resumed instance, 2026-09-14): the fix is worth 40 MORE rows
in t/op/universal.t, found by the round's op/ companion leg -- 82/62 -> 122/22.
The shape is the same one uni/universal.t has, in ASCII: a 7x7 matrix at
op/universal.t:106,
    is UNIVERSAL::isa($vals[$p], $refs[$q]), ($p==$q or $p+$q==1);
whose 40 false cells compare against '' and so failed on DEFINEDNESS while
truthiness agreed.  The whole 49-cell matrix is byte-identical to perl 5.40.3
now and reads UNDEF on an edd6dc78 extraction (probe both directions,
scratch/s473t5f/probe-isa-matrix.pl in the round's worktree).  40 CAUSELESS
blessed rows left baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv by edit (60 -> 20 for the
file); the snapshot row carries the cause.
subject: isa/DOES returned undef for FALSE where perl returns the empty string (PL_sv_no) -- 40 of t/uni/universal.t 49-row matrix; p-isa is boolean-valued now and the undef guard is perl own, in UNIVERSAL::isa (FIXED s473t5f)
